name: Investment Residence Permit (Real Estate or Business)

requirements.blocker_text: A minimum real-estate investment (a specific figure was not confirmed at tier-1 precision -- see notes) qualifies a foreign investor to apply for a long-term or renewable residence permit.

Secondary sources cite figures ranging from roughly USD 50,000 to USD 300,000 depending on the specific program/route, with explicit caution that these are not interchangeable across routes and requirements have evolved since 2023 policy amendments.

Investors can obtain a residence permit by establishing a company and depositing a minimum of EGP 100,000 in capital, though the framework emphasizes the legitimacy and seriousness of the project over a fixed threshold alone.
requirements.fix_path: Register a qualifying company and deposit the required capital.

evidence_required.document: Property purchase deed or company incorporation and capital deposit records

outcome.duration_length: Company route: 1 year initial, renewal tied to project implementation; real estate route duration not confirmed at tier-1 precision

sources.title: The Official Egyptian Real Estate Platform (Ministry-affiliated, realestate.gov.eg) -- Legal Guide for Foreigners Buying Property in Egypt: confirms foreigners investing a minimum amount, including real estate, can apply for long-term/renewable residence permits; foreign ownership capped at 2 residential properties, max 4,000 sqm combined; notes the government is actively working on legislation to ease investor residency

Youssry Saleh Law Firm -- Residency by Investment in Egypt: cites EGP 100,000 minimum for the company-capital route and a commonly-referenced but explicitly-cautioned USD 300,000 real-estate figure, notes 2023 policy amendments changed conditions

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Egypt). STATUS: DRAFT -- this is a genuinely unsettled area of Egyptian policy as of this research pass. The tier-1 government real-estate portal confirms the real-estate-to-residence-permit route EXISTS and is even actively being expanded by pending legislation, but states no concrete minimum figure. Secondary sources cite wildly different numbers for the real-estate threshold (USD 50,000 vs USD 300,000 depending on the source), with one explicitly warning against treating any single figure as universal across sub-routes -- modeled the existence as hard:true/tier-1 and the specific amount as hard:false/tier-3 with the conflict disclosed rather than resolved by picking one number. The company-formation route (EGP 100,000 capital) is comparatively more concrete but still only tier-3 sourced. citizenship_after_months (60) is a rough estimate assuming this route might access a shortened residence-based naturalization path similar to Article 4's 5-year 'Egyptian origin' provision (see eg_naturalisation.json) -- NOT confirmed as applicable to investors specifically, flagged as speculative rather than sourced.
